note: Ps94 God of vengeance / plea against wicked oppressors (23v). Passages: plea to the God of vengeance v1-7; rebuke of the senseless (he who planted the ear, hears) v8-11; blessed is the disciplined man v12-15; who stands up for me? the LORD held me up v16-19; can wicked rulers ally with you? the LORD is my stronghold v20-23. IB: the PROUD/WICKED who EXULT, speak ARROGANTly, CRUSH/AFFLICT/KILL/MURDER the helpless; the call to UNDERSTAND (FOOLS, be WISE); man's THOUGHTS known to be breath; BLESSED is the disciplined man given REST; the RIGHTEOUS/UPRIGHT in HEART; the SOUL near silence, the anxious CARES God's consolations cheer the SOUL; wicked rulers who frame INJUSTICE, BAND-TOGETHER, CONDEMN the INNOCENT; their INIQUITY/WICKEDNESS. God's vengeance/judge/discipline/teach/not-forsake/stronghold = qualifiers; pit/silence/statute imagery = standalone.

dims.v: v2: 'repay to the PROUD (geeh) what they deserve!' - the arrogant oppressors, pride that invites God's requital.
v3: 'How long shall the WICKED (rasha), O LORD, how long shall the wicked exult?' - the godless whose long triumph provokes the cry for vengeance.
v3: 'how long shall the wicked EXULT (alaz)?' - the wicked's arrogant triumph, gloating that seems to go unpunished.
v4: 'They speak ARROGANTLY (athaq); all the evildoers boast' - the insolent speech of the wicked, pride pouring from the mouth.
v5: 'They CRUSH (daka) your people, O LORD' - the violent oppression of the wicked against God's own.
v5: 'and AFFLICT (anah) your heritage' - the tormenting of God's inheritance by the wicked.
v6: 'They KILL (harag) the widow and the sojourner' - the murder of the defenceless, oppression at its cruelest.
v6: 'and MURDER (ratsach) the fatherless' - the slaying of the orphan, the wicked's contempt for the helpless.
paired with the call to be wise
v8: 'UNDERSTAND (bin), O dullest of the people!' - the summons to the brutish to consider, the call to sense.
paired with the call to be wise
v8: 'FOOLS (kesil), when will you be wise?' - the senseless who think God does not see, folly rebuked.
v8: 'when will you be WISE (sakal)?' - the wisdom the fools are urged toward, the discernment they lack.
known by God to be breath
v11: 'The LORD knows the THOUGHTS (machashabah) of man, that they are but a breath' - the vain reasonings of man, all exposed to God and shown to be nothing.
paired with being taught God's law
v12: 'BLESSED (esher) is the man whom you discipline, O LORD' - the happiness of the one God corrects and teaches, chastening as grace.
paired with the pit dug for the wicked
v13: 'to give him REST (shaqat) from days of trouble' - the quiet God grants the disciplined while judgment ripens for the wicked.
paired with the upright in heart
v15: 'for justice will return to the RIGHTEOUS (tsedeq)' - the righteous to whom judgment will come back round, vindication assured.
v15: 'and all the UPRIGHT (yashar) in heart will follow it' - the upright who pursue the returning justice, aligned with God's verdict.
v15: 'all the upright in HEART (leb) will follow it' - the inner rectitude of the upright, uprightness seated in the heart.
v17: 'my SOUL (nephesh) would soon have lived in the land of silence' - the self on the brink of death, saved only because God was his help.
v19: 'When the CARES (sarapp) of my heart are many' - the crowding anxieties within, the multiplied worries God meets with comfort.
v19: 'your consolations CHEER my SOUL (nephesh)' - the self gladdened by God's comforts, anxiety answered by divine consolation.
paired with framing injustice by statute
v20: 'Can WICKED (havvah) rulers be allied with you?' - the corrupt authorities who legislate evil, wickedness enthroned.
v20: 'those who frame INJUSTICE (amal) by statute?' - the manufacture of oppression under colour of law, evil made legal.
v21: 'They BAND TOGETHER (gadad) against the life of the righteous' - the conspiracy of the wicked, malice organized against the just.
v21: 'and CONDEMN (rasha) the innocent to death' - the judicial murder of the guiltless, the wicked's verdict against the blameless.
v21: 'and condemn the INNOCENT (naqi) to death' - the guiltless victim, whose very innocence the wicked assail.
v23: 'He will bring back on them their INIQUITY (aven)' - the guilt of the wicked, returned upon their own heads.
for which they are wiped out
v23: 'and wipe them out for their WICKEDNESS (ra)' - the evil for which the wicked are destroyed, sin recoiling on the sinner.
